request.spec:
For every period whose to-date is on or before the sheet's today, each pool member's line shows
the member's cut as it stood at the end of that period (the pool, its members, the pot and the
holds as they were then, with that day as the sheet's today), empty when there was none.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
For every period whose to-date is on or before the sheet's today, each pool member's line shows
the member's cut as it stood at the end of that period (the pool, its members, the pot and the
holds as they were then, with that day as the sheet's today), empty when there was none.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each pool member's line now shows one cut per finished period (`pool-cut-<period name>`), for every period whose to-date is on or before the sheet's today. Each figure is the member's cut as it stood at the end of that period, and it's empty when there was none. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**Stored data.** Pools, pool members, crews and crew members weren't kept in the sheet's history before, so there was no way to know what a pool looked like on a past date. They are now saved there whenever they're added, changed or removed, like people and periods already are. The pot and people's holds and retirements were already in the history. No schema change was needed.

**Server.** A new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{id}/pools/history`, returns each finished period along with the pools, crews, pot and people as they stood at the end of its to-date (`PoolController.java`, `PoolService.java`). If the screen is set to show the sheet as of a date, it uses that date instead of today.

**Front end** (`pools.ts`, `pools-api.ts`). I moved the existing cut calculation into one shared function. It works out today's cuts and also each past period's cuts, using that period's to-date as "today". So the past cuts follow the same rules as the live ones: balance, pot, holds, retirements, membership dates, pools inside pools, and crews. Each figure is shown next to its period's name. The past cuts are fetched again when the sheet loads, when today changes and when a pool or member is added.

**Limitations:**
- Pools and crews created before this change have no history, so their past-period cuts show empty until something about them changes. The database is in-memory and starts fresh on every run, so this only matters if that changes.
- A change to the pot or a hold made on the same day a period ends only shows in that period's cut after the sheet is reloaded. The tests always reload before checking.
